justifications.functional_suitability: R-01 (catalogue physical & digital items) has no dedicated catalogue or circulation container. Search Container only indexes data via CDC with no source of truth. Circulation and notifications appear only at context level. Cataloguing is largely unaddressed.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Search Container uses horizontally scalable Elasticsearch/OpenSearch with asynchronous CDC and Kafka/Fluentbit telemetry, plus rate limiting in the API Gateway. No caching, no capacity or latency measurement, and no load-testing mechanism for the 800 ms p99 target; the claim is asserted only.
justifications.compatibility: External ILS / Book Supplier Integration uses mTLS with JWT/HMAC, and OAuth2/OIDC, OpenAPI and W3C Trace Context are standards. However, no container owns the external integrations; the relationships originate from the system boundary, and the Notification Gateway uses an unspecified 'API'.
justifications.usability: Web UI and Accessibility Layer offers WCAG 2.1 AA with axe-core and error boundaries for patrons, staff and admins. But one Self-Service Portal serves all groups, with no distinct librarian circulation interface, and the DPO dashboard is only a component.
justifications.reliability: Kafka DLQ, LUKS spillover buffering and Prometheus monitoring exist, and the Search Container is horizontally scalable. There is no replication, failover, backup/recovery, health checks, circuit breakers or availability targets, and the single API Gateway is a single point of failure.
justifications.security: Layered controls: OAuth2/OIDC Token Validator, WAF Input Sanitizer, mTLS via SPIFFE/SPIRE, RBAC SSO and MFA, and CSP with secure cookies. Audit & Compliance Container adds EU-localized HSM, WORM Storage, Merkle Tree tamper evidence and SIEM alerts, plus document-level access control in the Search API Handler.
justifications.maintainability: Containers and components have clear responsibilities, and the gateway pipeline is modular. However, the model has self-referential relationships, actors modelled as components, a duplicated container inside its own component view, and no catalogue or circulation modules, which weakens coherence.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes and open-source OpenSearch/Kafka are portable, but the model has no explicit deployment view, no IaC or containerization of all parts, and the EU-localized HSM and 'local cloud region' tie it to specific infrastructure with no replaceability strategy.

sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cluster sizing for 2,000 concurrent searches
Gateway rate limiting may throttle legitimate semester-start bursts
tradeoffs: Gateway security layers add latency versus the 800 ms budget
PERF-01.justification: Horizontally scalable search engine and a dedicated gateway route exist, but there is no caching, autoscaling, replica or load-test mechanism. The 800 ms target is only asserted, not demonstrated.

sensitivity_points: Indexing load competes with search queries
tradeoffs: Asynchronous CDC gives search isolation but eventual consistency
PERF-02.justification: Async CDC ingestion decouples writes from search and plausibly meets 5 minutes. But no catalogue/circulation source container is modelled, the CDC source is a self-loop, and there is no index/query isolation.

sensitivity_points: Replica and shard configuration is unspecified
No failover detection or recovery is modelled
tradeoffs: Replication improves availability but adds cost and indexing overhead
AVAIL-01.justification: Horizontal scalability implies a cluster, but replicas and failover are not explicit. No circulation or loan transaction store is modelled, so lost loan transactions cannot be assessed.

sensitivity_points: Portal instance redundancy and load balancing not specified
Session state handling across instances unclear
tradeoffs: Stateless cookie sessions ease failover but limit server-side revocation
AVAIL-02.justification: The portal is a single container with no stated replicas, load balancer or health checks. Loan management has no backing container, so no-loss transactions are not addressed.

sensitivity_points: No integration or adapter component for providers
tradeoffs: A single external integration point is simple but not extensible
MOD-01.justification: Only a generic external ILS/supplier link exists, with no internal integration component or adapter abstraction. Adding an e-book provider would require unclear changes, so confinement to one component is not shown.

sensitivity_points: No circulation or loan rules component exists
MOD-02.justification: The architecture has no circulation service, rules engine or configuration store. Runtime configurable loan rules per library type cannot be achieved with the existing elements.

sensitivity_points: External systems' hosting regions are unspecified
Telemetry pseudonymization is claimed but not enforced
tradeoffs: EU-only constraints limit use of global SaaS services
SEC-01.justification: EU-localized HSM and an audit container address residency, but it is stated rather than enforced by design. External notification, analytics and SIEM systems have no EU guarantee, and there is no region-enforcement mechanism.

sensitivity_points: No loan history service enforces object-level authorization
Denied-access event logging path is unclear
tradeoffs: Strict gateway checks add latency but strengthen security
SEC-02.justification: Strong authentication, RBAC and tamper-evident audit logging exist. However, no loan data component enforces per-patron ownership checks, and the denied attempt logging is not explicitly modelled.
